Ports number 0-23 in one range, the four QSFP28s first.","format":1,"gaps":[{"reason":"sources-disagree","scope":["front","rear","top","bottom","left","right"],"wanted":"A third statement. csr430-datasheet says \"440 x 300 x 44 mm\" and 5.44 kg; csr430-qsg's hardware specification says \"438.4 x 300 x 43.7 mm\" and 5.42 kg. Both are single-model documents for the AS7515-24X, so this is not a shared quick start describing a sibling. The datasheet is taken because the figure's measured aspect of 9.9091 sits nearer 10.0 than 10.0320, and because the CSR310 - which the programme records as sharing this shell - states 440 x 300 x 44 in BOTH its documents. That is three statements against one, and it is still a disagreement rather than a resolution.","what":"chassis-dimensions"},{"reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["front"],"wanted":"A part number for this device's fan tray. The CSR430's datasheet carries no field-replacement table; its quick start describes replacing the tray without naming it. edgecore/csr310-fan-tray@1 is fitted here on the strength of the DRAWING ALONE - handle, AIRFLOW arrow and thumbscrew within about two millimetres on both elevations, which is the noise floor at 8-9 px/mm. The supplies are shared on much better evidence, a part number stated in this device's own quick start. This one is an identification, not a proof, and a part number would settle it either way.","what":"fan-tray-part-number"},{"reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["rear","top","bottom","left","right"],"wanted":"A figure of any face but the front, which on this device is a smaller hole than usual and is worth saying why. The datasheet's key features include \"All ports, PSUs and fan modules are front access\" and \"Maintenance activity to replace PSUs and FANs can be done from the front panel without remove the product from rack\" - so the rear carries no user hardware at all. The quick start's callout 11 is a \"Grounding screw\"; it is not located, so it is not placed. The SIDE panels carry the intake and exhaust on a side-to-side box and no figure shows either. Per docs/deliberately-empty-faces.md these faces are DECLARED empty with the reason rather than left silent, which is the difference between empty-by-verification and empty-by-omission.","what":"rear-elevation"},{"reason":"needs-photo","scope":["front"],"wanted":"What the white perforated strip between each QSFP28 cage pair is. On the SFP28 columns the equivalent strip carries one arrow lamp per port and three vent holes, and the quick start's LED table names the arrow lamps' colours. Between the QSFP cages the strip is a dense grid of rectangular openings with no arrows - it reads as a vent, and the QSFP ports' own lamps are the rectangles in the silkscreen band below, which is where the numerals put them. It is drawn as a vent on that reading; a photograph would confirm there is no lamp in it.","what":"qsfp-bezel-content"}],"groups":{"fans":{"attrs":{"redundancy-note":"\"4+1 redundant fans, hot-swappable fan tray\" and \"4+1 high-efficiency modular fans\", both verbatim from the datasheet - FIVE FANS INSIDE ONE REPLACEABLE TRAY. NO `redundancy` FORM IS SET, and the reason is structural rather than evidential. A digit form in this library describes BAYS - spec/tests/test_fan_redundancy.py checks that the parts of `N+M` sum to the number of bays in the group - and this group has one bay, the tray, with the five fans inside it. Writing `4+1` against one bay would state a true fact at the wrong level and make a rule that is right in general fire on a device it is wrong about; writing `n+1` would be vaguer than the document. THE STRUCTURALLY CORRECT ANSWER IS NESTED BAYS - five fan positions inside the tray module - and the figure does not support it: the tray is drawn closed, with a handle, an arrow and a thumbscrew and no grille, so five positions would be invented. Nest them the day a figure of the tray's interior turns up."},"index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"Fan"},"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"leds":{"index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the management cluster - the 1000BASE-T RJ-45 and the RS-232 console share one bezel, and the USB-A storage port and the Reset button sit with the timing jacks. The quick start adds the rule that makes it matter: \"Install replacement tray with matching airflow direction.\""},"chassis":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"THE TWO DOCUMENTS DISAGREE, and it is recorded in gaps as sources-disagree rather than averaged. The datasheet says \"440 x 300 x 44 mm\" and 5.44 kg; the quick start's hardware specification says \"438.4 x 300 x 43.7 mm\" and 5.42 kg. The datasheet is taken, for two reasons that are both checkable. THE FIGURE PREFERS IT: the panel's measured aspect of 9.9091 sits nearer 10.0 (440/44) than 10.0320 (438.4/43.7), 0.91 percent against 1.23. AND THE SIBLING THAT SHARES THIS SHELL STATES IT TWICE: the CSR310's datasheet and quick start both give 440 x 300 x 44, so three documents say 440 x 44 and one says otherwise. The depth is not in dispute."},"figure-choice":{"confidence":"measured","note":"Gate 1, and there are two candidates because the page draws the device twice. The DC elevation wins: panel (518,2885)-(4441,3280), 3924 x 396 px, aspect 9.9091 against 10.0 for 440/44 - 0.91 percent out. The AC elevation above it detects at 3926 x 372, aspect 10.55, because its supplies are pale and the row-darkness scan clips the band short; its WIDTH is 3926 against the DC figure's 3924, agreeing to 0.05 percent. SO THE TWO FIGURES SHARE ONE X SCALE, 8.9182 px/mm, and an x measured on one is an x on the other. That is what lets the AC supply's face be read from the upper figure and placed with the lower figure's coordinates, rather than one being assumed from the other."},"lamps":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"THE QUICK START HAS A REAL LED TABLE, WHICH NO OTHER DEVICE IN THIS FAMILY HAS GIVEN. System: \"LOC - Blinking Blue (device locator) DIAG - Green (OK), Orange (fault detected) PSU1/2 - Green (OK), Amber (fault) FAN - Green (OK), Orange (fault)\". Ports: \"QSFP28 Port LEDs: Green - 100G, Cyan - 50G, Magenta - 40G, Blue - 25G, Yellow - 10G\" and \"SFP28 Port LEDs: Blue - 25G, Green - 10G, Cyan - 1G\". And the management jack: \"Left (link), Right (activity)\". So every lamp here carries a stated vocabulary and there is no led-vocabularies gap. IT ALSO SETTLES WHAT THE BEZEL MARKS ARE. Each SFP28 column prints `(up) o o o (down)` between its rows: ONE lamp per port - the arrow, pointing at the row it serves, as on the AGR110 and CSR200 - with three round vent holes between them, not five lamps. One lamp per port is what a single speed vocabulary describes."},"optical-blocks":{"confidence":"measured","note":"THE SFP28 BANK IS IN TWO GROUPS, NOT ONE, and a column of vent holes separates them. Ports 4-11 sit in four columns from 181.08 and ports 12-23 in six from 245.90, with 7.8 mm of perforated metal between - so it is modelled as two blocks sharing one group rather than as a ten-column comb with an invented uniform gutter. Both are anchored on measured centres and sized from the registry, and the two agree: the bezel arrows put column 1 at 188.2 and the numerals put the last column at 324.5 against 324.3 predicted. The QSFP28 shells centre on 139.10 and 164.65, a 25.55 pitch on an 18.5 cage, so 7.05 of gutter."},"port-numbering":{"confidence":"measured","note":"ONE RANGE, 0 TO 23, WITH THE QSFP28s FIRST - simpler than the CSR310's three spaces and read the same way, off the numerals under the cages. The four 100G cages are numbered 0, 1, 2, 3 and the twenty 25G columns run 4/5 through 22/23, each column printing `n (up)(down) n+1` on one baseline."},"psus-and-fans":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"ALL THREE FIELD-REPLACEABLE UNITS ARE THE CSR310's, AND THE DC SUPPLY IS PROVEN SO BY PART NUMBER: this device's own quick start says \"Install one or two DC PSUs (part number CRXT-T0T12B only)\", which is the sentence the CSR310's quick start carries. The faces were then read off both elevations against one rule and agree inside the precision of art at 8-9 px/mm - warning triangles at 23.0/22.9 and 40.3/40.8, terminal block 29.6/30.0 wide with poles at 16.7/25.9/36.5 and 16.7/25.9/35.6. THE FAN TRAY IS WEAKER AND IS CARRIED AS A GAP. No part number exists for it here: the CSR430's datasheet has no field-replacement table where the CSR310's names FAN-1U-1x1J-S. The identification is by drawing alone - handle, AIRFLOW arrow and thumbscrew all within about two millimetres - which is the noise floor rather than a match. Bays: the supplies at 4.64 and 67.74, a 63.1 pitch taken from the warning triangles printed on the modules rather than from their edges, because a triangle is a mark and an edge is a shadow. The tray runs 394.9 to the panel edge."},"sources":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"Two documents, both staged and both docling-converted, MEASURED OFF THE PDF PAGE RATHER THAN THE CONVERTED FIGURES. csr430-datasheet carries the specification list, the eleven-callout interface table, and TWO front elevations on page 2 - one with AC supplies fitted and one with DC - which is more than any other device in this family gives and is why both configurations are drawn from measurement rather than one from the other. csr430-qsg carries no figure worth measuring and supplies the names: the callout list, the FRU procedures, the DC supply's part number, and - uniquely in this family so far - A REAL LED TABLE."},"stack-orientation":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the port lamps, which point up over down: the 10 SFP pairs (port-4/port-5 to port-22/port-23). Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 2 QSFP pairs (port-0/port-1 and port-2/port-3)."}},"references":[{"sha256":"61695d498c504c3224190b9742e78411ecb960970ece9a2ba970a59fab3b7c38","title":"Edgecore CSR430 / AS7515-24X Cell Site Router Data Sheet"},{"sha256":"c892efca83863522cfbabccf371363d1645f0896b3f50ba2b6d16767a491f110","title":"Edgecore AS7515-24X Cell Site Gateway Quick Start Guide"}],"version":"1.0.5","views":{"bottom":{"empty":"Not drawn by any staged source.
